subject: Cooking
title: Emulsions: How Oil and Water Mix
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Emulsions: How Oil and Water Mix.

hook.text: Oil and water don't mix — unless you know the trick. Mayonnaise is that trick perfected.

buildup.text: An emulsion forces tiny droplets of one liquid to suspend inside another using violent agitation.

discovery.text: Egg yolk's lecithin acts as an emulsifier — one end grabs oil, the other grabs water.

twist.text: Add oil too fast and the emulsion 'breaks' — lecithin gets overwhelmed and droplets re-separate.

climax.text: Vinaigrette, hollandaise, and even milk are all emulsions held together by molecular bridges.

punchline.text: Emulsifiers don't mix oil and water. They broker peace.

quiz.question: What role does lecithin from egg yolk play in mayonnaise?

details.summary: Emulsions suspend tiny droplets of one liquid in another that normally would not mix, like oil in water. Emulsifiers such as lecithin in egg yolks coat each droplet, preventing separation. Mayonnaise, vinaigrettes, and hollandaise are all emulsions held together by molecular bridges.
details.whyItMatters: Emulsions are behind many classic sauces and dressings. Knowing how they form and break helps you create stable, creamy textures and rescue split sauces.
takeaways: Emulsifiers coat oil droplets to prevent them from merging
Egg yolk lecithin is the most common kitchen emulsifier
Temperature shocks and excess fat can break emulsions

faq.question: Why does mayonnaise sometimes split?
faq.answer: Adding oil too fast overwhelms the emulsifier, causing droplets to merge and separate. Temperature extremes also break emulsions. To rescue split mayo, whisk a fresh yolk and slowly stream the broken mixture into it, rebuilding the emulsion one drop at a time.

faq.question: What other emulsifiers exist besides egg yolk?
faq.answer: Mustard contains mucilage that stabilizes vinaigrettes. Garlic acts as an emulsifier in aioli. Soy lecithin is used in commercial products. Xanthan gum and gum arabic are modern stabilizers. Even pasta water starch emulsifies sauce with olive oil.
